title: Good or Bad? 6 Fruits in 90 Seconds
sources_note: Nutrition per USDA FoodData Central (approx., rounded). Prices: approx. US average retail, USDA ERS fruit price data; vary by region/season.

sentences.text: Six fruits.
Are they good or bad for your body, and what do they really cost?
Let's crack them open.
Banana.
About a hundred and five calories, three grams of fiber, and over four hundred milligrams of potassium for your muscles and heart.
Verdict: good. A perfect fuel before a workout.
Cost? About twenty five cents each.
Apple.
Ninety five calories and over four grams of fiber, and most of the good stuff lives in the skin, so don't peel it.
Verdict: good. It keeps you full for hours.
Around ninety cents an apple.
Avocado.
Packed with heart healthy fats and nine grams of fiber. But one whole avocado is over two hundred calories.
Verdict: good, in portions. Half is plenty.
About a dollar twenty five each.
Blueberries.
Just eighty four calories a cup, and loaded with antioxidants that help protect your brain and blood vessels.
Verdict: excellent. The best health value on this list.
Roughly four dollars a pint.
Orange.
One gives you nearly a full day of vitamin C, plus the fiber that juice throws away.
Verdict: good. Eat it, don't drink it.
About seventy five cents each.
Mango.
Rich in vitamins A and C, but one whole mango carries over forty grams of sugar.
Verdict: watch out. Stick to one cup.
About a dollar each.
Best overall? Blueberries.
